200.q: Brazilian striker with a ferocious left foot. Starred for Inter Milan in the mid-2000s and was known as the Emperor. Was top scorer and best player at the 2004 Copa America.
Brazilian forward built like a bodybuilder with a rocket left foot. Won titles at Porto, then moved to Zenit St Petersburg and later to Shanghai. His comic-book nickname stuck for life.
Brazilian attacking midfielder who joined Chelsea in 2012 and won the Premier League in 2015. Scored his country's only goal in the 7-1 defeat to Germany. Left for a huge fee to Shanghai in 2017.
Brazilian winger who joined Chelsea from Anzhi in 2013 and won two Premier League titles. Renowned for curling free kicks. Left on a free for Arsenal in 2020 and later played for Fulham.

Brazilian holding midfielder signed from Shakhtar Donetsk in 2013. Anchored Manchester City's midfield through five title wins and captained the side late in his spell. Returned home to Athletico Paranaense in 2022.
Brazilian winger who scored a hat-trick in Amsterdam to send Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final. Joined from PSG in 2018 and later returned to Sao Paulo.

Brazilian winger known for lightning dribbling and stepovers. Won league titles in Ukraine, Germany and Italy with Shakhtar, Bayern Munich and Juventus. Joined Bayern in 2015 and moved to Turin two years later.
Brazilian winger who joined Manchester United from Ajax in 2022 for around 82 million pounds. Struggled in England and revived his career on loan at Real Betis. Known for spinning on the ball.

Brazilian forward who agreed to join Real Madrid from Palmeiras as a 16-year-old and arrived once he turned 18 in 2024. Scored the winner against England at Wembley on his first start for his country.
Brazilian centre-back who joined Real Madrid from Porto in 2019. Won the Champions League in 2022 and 2024 either side of serious knee injuries. Wears number 3 at the Bernabeu.
Brazilian centre-back signed by Arsenal from Lille in 2020. A constant threat from corners and a regular scorer of headers. Formed a first-choice partnership with a young French defender.

French forward who became the world's most expensive teenager when Manchester United signed him from Monaco in 2015. Scored a slaloming solo goal on his debut against Liverpool. Left on a free transfer in 2024.
French striker who joined Arsenal from Lyon in 2017 for a then club-record fee. Returned to his boyhood club in 2022 and captained them. Known for a low centre of gravity and clinical finishing.

French midfielder who came through at Marseille, moved to Arsenal in 2008 and then to Manchester City in 2011, winning two Premier League titles. Served a doping ban in 2018 over an intravenous drip treatment.

Spanish midfielder equally comfortable with both feet. Won two FA Cups with Arsenal before a leg infection nearly cost him his foot. Fought back to play again for Villarreal and later returned to his boyhood club Oviedo.

Spanish midfielder who played for Rangers, Everton and Arsenal, captaining the last of those before retiring in 2016. Became Guardiola's assistant at Manchester City, then went back to manage the club he had captained.
Belgian centre-back who spent eight years at Tottenham after leaving Ajax. Became his country's most-capped player. Finished his career at Anderlecht.
Belgian forward who became Napoli's all-time leading scorer after being converted from winger to striker. Small, quick and a fine free-kick taker. Joined Galatasaray in 2022.
German winger who scored four goals at Tottenham in a 2019 Champions League group game for Bayern Munich. Earlier had a forgettable loan spell at West Brom while on Arsenal's books.
German striker signed by Chelsea from RB Leipzig in 2020. Famous for blistering pace and a habit of missing big chances. Won the Champions League in 2021, then returned to Germany.
German midfielder who joined Bayern Munich from Schalke on a free transfer in 2018. Famous for a dramatic muscle transformation during lockdown. Scored a late equaliser against Hungary at Euro 2020.
German midfielder who won the 2014 World Cup. Joined Real Madrid from Stuttgart in 2010 and later moved to Juventus on a free, winning five straight Serie A titles. Finished at Hertha Berlin.

German striker and a classic penalty-box poacher. Won multiple Bundesliga titles with Bayern Munich after joining from Stuttgart in 2009. Later played for Fiorentina and Besiktas before ending his career back in Stuttgart.
Portuguese centre-back who followed Mourinho from Porto to Chelsea in 2004. Won the 2004 Champions League and three Premier League titles, then joined Real Madrid. Won Euro 2016 at the age of 38.
Spanish forward with a wand of a left foot. Scored in the 2017 Champions League final for Real Madrid. Left the club on a free transfer for PSG in 2023.
Spanish midfielder and Atletico Madrid's record appearance holder. Captains the club he joined as a child. Spent years supplying assists to Diego Costa and Griezmann.

Spanish winger from the Barcelona academy who scored in six different competitions in a single calendar year. Joined Chelsea in 2015 and won the title in his first season. Later played for Roma and Lazio.
Spanish forward who left Valencia for Manchester City in 2020 and joined Barcelona a year later for around 55 million euros. Scored a hat-trick against Germany in a 6-0 Nations League rout in 2020.
Guinea-Bissau-born forward for Spain who became Barcelona's youngest ever goalscorer at 16. Inherited the number 10 shirt after Messi left. Injuries stalled him and he moved to Monaco in 2025.
Ivorian winger and Crystal Palace's talisman for a decade. An early move to Manchester United in 2013 did not work out and he returned to Selhurst Park. Joined Galatasaray on a free in 2023.
Ghanaian midfielder whose release clause was triggered by Arsenal on deadline day in 2020. Previously won the Europa League and La Liga with Atletico Madrid. Known for driving runs from deep.

Cameroonian goalkeeper who came through Barcelona's academy, then starred for Ajax and reached the 2023 Champions League final with Inter. Joined Manchester United that summer. Known for aggressive distribution.

Senegalese goalkeeper who was without a club a few years before signing for Chelsea in 2020. Won the Champions League in his first season and the Africa Cup of Nations in 2022. Moved to Al-Ahli in 2023.

Ukrainian who arrived at Manchester City as an attacking midfielder and was converted into an inverted left-back. Won four Premier League titles before joining Arsenal in 2022. Became a prominent voice for his country after the 2022 invasion.

Swedish attacking player born in Stockholm to Macedonian parents. Broke through on loan at Parma, joined Juventus, then moved to Tottenham in 2022. Powerful on the right wing, cutting inside onto his left.

Danish striker signed by Manchester United from Atalanta in 2023 for around 72 million pounds. Scored in five straight Champions League group games during a long league drought. Joined Napoli in 2025.
Mexican striker who fractured his skull in a clash of heads at Arsenal in 2020 and returned wearing protective headgear. Starred for Wolves after a spell at Benfica. Joined Fulham in 2024.
Mexican winger who scored the goal that beat holders Germany at the 2018 World Cup. Joined Napoli from PSV and won the 2023 Scudetto. Nicknamed Chucky for frightening his team-mates as a youngster.

Mexican forward who never quite broke through at Arsenal but starred for Real Sociedad. Set an MLS single-season scoring record with 34 goals for LAFC in 2019. Often turned down national team call-ups.

American striker who retired in 2015 as the all-time leading international goalscorer for either gender with 184. Scored a famous last-minute header against Brazil at the 2011 World Cup. Won two Olympic golds.

400.q: American midfielder who scored a 16-minute hat-trick in the 2015 World Cup final, including a strike from the halfway line. Also scored the winning goals in the 2008 and 2012 Olympic finals.

English right-back who won the Champions League three times with Lyon and later played for Barcelona and Chelsea. Won Euro 2022 with her country. Revealed she played through the 2025 Euros with a fractured tibia.
Dutch striker who is the Women's Super League all-time leading scorer. Once scored six in a single Arsenal league game. Won Euro 2017 with her country and joined Manchester City in 2024.
French centre-back born on Martinique who stands 1.87m tall. Captained Lyon to eight Champions League titles and was a huge aerial threat from set pieces.

English forward who won the Golden Boot and player of the tournament award at Euro 2022. An Arsenal winger who missed the following World Cup with a knee injury. Won BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2022.
English defender who captained her country to the Euro 2022 title at Wembley. An Arsenal one-club player used at centre-back and in midfield. Missed the 2023 World Cup with a ruptured knee ligament.

Japanese midfielder who captained her country to the 2011 World Cup and scored the late equaliser in the final against the United States. Won the Golden Ball and Golden Boot there and was named world player of the year.
German striker who won the World Cup in 2003 and 2007 and was named FIFA World Player of the Year three years running. Long her country's record scorer and a Frankfurt stalwart.
Brazilian left-footed midfielder from the 1970 World Cup-winning side. Famous for a thunderous free kick and a bushy moustache. Popularised the flip-flap dribble later used by Ronaldinho.
Brazilian right-back who captained the 1970 World Cup winners and finished off the tournament's most celebrated team goal in the final against Italy. Later played for the New York Cosmos.
Brazilian forward who partnered Pele in the 1970 World Cup win. A detached retina forced him to retire at 26, after which he became a doctor and a newspaper columnist.
Brazilian striker who played alongside Maradona at Napoli and won the UEFA Cup there in 1989. Was his country's top scorer at the 1986 World Cup with five goals.
Brazilian goalkeeper who made a save in the 1994 World Cup final shoot-out against Italy. Later played for Galatasaray and became Liverpool's goalkeeping coach.
Brazilian right-back who won the 2010 treble with Inter Milan and scored from a near-impossible angle against North Korea at that year's World Cup. Later played for Manchester City and Roma.
Brazilian holding midfielder nicknamed the Invisible Wall. Won the 2002 World Cup and was part of Arsenal's unbeaten league season. Later played for Panathinaikos.
Mexican goalkeeper famous for designing his own garish kits and for standing only about 1.68m tall. Sometimes played as a forward for his club. Appeared at the 1994 and 1998 World Cups.
Mexican forward who invented a trick of trapping the ball between his feet and hopping past defenders. Played at three World Cups and later became a state governor.
Mexican midfielder who appeared at five World Cups. Spent seven years as a leader at Real Betis, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022. Earlier played for Deportivo, Valencia and PSV.
Chilean striker nicknamed the Matador. Scored twice against England at Wembley in 1998, then starred at that year's World Cup. Played for River Plate, Lazio and Juventus.
Colombian midfielder who scored a late equaliser against West Germany at the 1990 World Cup. Powerfully built and a captain of his country. Also played for Real Madrid, Napoli and Palmeiras.
Uruguayan forward with a fearsome left foot who spent a decade at Inter Milan. Scored twice as a substitute on his Serie A debut in 1997. At one point among the best-paid players in the world.
Uruguayan goalkeeper who spent more than a decade as Galatasaray's number one. Was in goal as his country finished fourth at the 2010 World Cup. Suffered a horrific leg break in 2019.

Uruguayan centre-back who joined Barcelona from a small club at home and became a defensive leader there. Known for raw pace and last-ditch tackles. Sent off against PSG in a 2024 Champions League quarter-final.

Argentine centre-back who captained his country to the 1978 World Cup and was also in the 1986 squad. Unusually prolific from set pieces and penalties. Later managed his national team and River Plate.

Argentine forward who scored in the 1986 World Cup final win over West Germany. Played for Real Madrid and later managed and became sporting director there. Known as football's philosopher for his writing.
Argentine playmaker of the 1990s known for mesmerising dribbling and a fiery temper. Sent off in the 1998 World Cup quarter-final for head-butting the Dutch goalkeeper. A River Plate idol.

Argentine midfielder who scored a stunning left-foot volley against Mexico in the 2006 World Cup last 16. Converted the winning penalty in the 2014 semi-final shoot-out against the Netherlands. Played for Atletico Madrid and Liverpool.
Argentine midfielder who won three Europa League titles with Sevilla across two spells. An elegant passer with a low centre of gravity. Moved to Al-Shabab in 2020.
Argentine centre-back nicknamed the Mouse. Won over 110 caps and played for Valencia, AC Milan and Zaragoza. Missed a penalty in the 2006 World Cup quarter-final shoot-out against Germany.
Argentine centre-back nicknamed the Wall for his uncompromising defending. Won the Scudetto with Roma in 2001 and the treble with Inter in 2010. Also had a spell at Real Madrid.
Argentine goalkeeper who won the 1978 World Cup on home soil and was voted the tournament's best keeper. A River Plate legend who saved a penalty in the group game against Poland.
French striker who won the 1991 Ballon d'Or while at Marseille, where he was the league's top scorer five years running. Famous for spectacular volleys. Later played for AC Milan and Bayern Munich.
French attacking midfielder who won the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000. Won the UEFA Cup with Inter in 1998. Later played for Kaiserslautern, Bolton and the New York Red Bulls.

French midfielder from New Caledonia who won the 1998 World Cup and two Champions Leagues with Real Madrid. Famously did not sing the anthem before matches. Later played for Middlesbrough and Olympiacos.
French centre-back who came into the 1998 World Cup final for a suspended team-mate and won the trophy. Spent five years at Chelsea, winning the Cup Winners' Cup. Became an actor after retiring.
French midfielder born in Bamako who was part of the celebrated magic square midfield that won Euro 1984. Starred for Bordeaux and Marseille. Later managed Fulham to promotion.
French box-to-box midfielder who won the 2018 World Cup. Won four league titles with PSG before joining Juventus in 2017. Finished his career at Inter Miami.
London-born winger who chose to represent France. Left Crystal Palace for Bayern Munich in 2024 and starred immediately. Left-footed on the right with elite set-piece delivery.
French forward who scored twice in the 2025 Champions League final for PSG and was named man of the match aged 19. Had joined from Rennes the previous summer.
Spanish striker who won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid, then knocked them out of the competition in 2004 while on loan at Monaco. Later played for Liverpool and Valencia.

600.q: Czechoslovak midfielder who won the 1962 Ballon d'Or and scored his country's goal in that year's World Cup final against Brazil. Spent most of his career at Dukla Prague.
Czech winger who scored a famous scooped lob against Portugal at Euro 96 and earned a move to Manchester United. His long hair and running earned him a nickname referencing an express train.
Czech striker who won the Golden Boot at Euro 2004 with five goals. Won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005. Later played for Aston Villa, Lyon and Galatasaray.
Soviet goalkeeper widely rated the world's best in 1988, the year his country reached the European Championship final. A Spartak Moscow icon who later played for Sevilla.
Russian goalkeeper and a one-club man at CSKA Moscow. Saved a penalty with his foot in the 2018 World Cup shoot-out to knock out Spain on home soil.
Ukrainian winger who left Dynamo Kyiv for Borussia Dortmund in 2017 and later played for West Ham. Left-footed on the right and one of his country's leading scorers.
Romanian centre-back who captained his country and played for Tottenham, Barcelona and Galatasaray. Scored the decisive penalty in the 2000 UEFA Cup final shoot-out.
Romanian right wing-back who scored the winning goal against England at the 1998 World Cup. Spent five years at Chelsea, winning the FA Cup and the Cup Winners' Cup.
Greek midfielder who captained his country to the shock Euro 2004 title and was named player of the tournament. Had a spell at Leicester City.
Greek centre-back whose header completed Roma's stunning 3-0 comeback against Barcelona in the 2018 Champions League quarter-final. Later joined Napoli.

Turkish goalkeeper with trademark black paint under his eyes and a ponytail. Starred as his country finished third at the 2002 World Cup. Spent most of his career at Fenerbahce with a season at Barcelona.
Turkish forward who scored twice in the last five minutes to beat the Czech Republic at Euro 2008. Starred for Real Sociedad, who nearly won La Liga in 2003.
Turkish striker who captained his country and helped Lille to a shock Ligue 1 title in 2021. Previously won several Turkish top-flight golden boots, mostly with Galatasaray.
Belgian playmaker of Italian descent who appeared at four World Cups between 1986 and 1998. Played for Anderlecht, Inter, Bordeaux and Monaco. Hailed as a new Pele as a teenager.
Belgian goalkeeper who starred as his country reached the 1986 World Cup semi-finals. Won three Bundesliga titles with Bayern Munich in the 1980s. Became a reality-TV personality at home.
Belgian midfielder with an unmistakable afro who joined Manchester United from Everton on deadline day in 2013. Used as a battering ram in the closing minutes. Left for China in 2019.
Belgian midfielder who played for Standard Liege, Benfica, Zenit and a Chinese club before joining Borussia Dortmund in 2018. Later moved to Atletico Madrid and was reinvented as a centre-back.
Belgian winger who joined Manchester City from Rennes in 2023. Came through at Anderlecht and made his international debut as a teenager. Explosive, low to the ground and hard to knock over.
Swiss goalkeeper who saved a penalty in the shoot-out that knocked France out of Euro 2020. Played for Borussia Monchengladbach, Bayern Munich and Inter.
Swiss right-back who won seven straight Serie A titles with Juventus. Nicknamed the Forrest Gump of football for his tireless running. Joined Arsenal in 2018.
Austrian forward who came through at Inter under Mourinho, then made his name at Stoke and West Ham. Captained his country and became its record goalscorer. Returned to Inter in 2023.
Austrian striker who scored twice as his country beat West Germany in the 1978 Miracle of Cordoba. Won the European Golden Boot that year and later played for Barcelona.
Swedish forward who starred as his country finished third at the 1994 World Cup, scoring from a clever free-kick routine against Romania. His later move to Leeds became a byword for a flop.
Danish winger who won Euro 1992 and became a hero at Rangers, where he was voted Scotland's player of the year in 1996. Also played for Fiorentina and AC Milan.
Danish striker who inspired unfashionable Hellas Verona to the 1985 Serie A title. Scored a hat-trick against Uruguay at the 1986 World Cup. Finished second in the 1984 Ballon d'Or.

Norwegian left-back with one of the hardest shots in the game. Scored a thunderous free kick against Manchester United at Anfield in his first season with Liverpool. Later scored a costly own goal against Chelsea in a 2008 semi-final.
Lanky Norwegian striker who scored the equaliser as his country beat Brazil at the 1998 World Cup. Played for Chelsea before a then Scottish-record move to Rangers.
Icelandic striker who once came on as a substitute for his own father in an international match. Won two Premier League titles with Chelsea and the 2009 Champions League with Barcelona.
Finnish striker who scored 29 goals to fire Norwich to the Championship title in 2019. His country's all-time top scorer, he led them to their first major tournament at Euro 2020.
Irish winger who moved from Blackburn to Chelsea in 2003 for a club-record fee and won two Premier League titles. Later played for Newcastle and Fulham, reaching the 2010 Europa League final.
Irish midfielder nicknamed Chippy for his love of chips rather than his passing. Won the 1979 FA Cup with Arsenal before seven years in Italy with Juventus, Sampdoria and Inter.
Irish goalkeeper who made over 350 Premier League appearances for Newcastle before joining Manchester City in 2009. Also played for Aston Villa and Stoke, winning more than 130 caps.
Australian striker who scored all four goals for Leeds in a 4-3 win over Liverpool in 2000. Captained his country at the 2006 World Cup. Also played for Celtic, Middlesbrough and Newcastle.
Australian goalkeeper who played over 500 Premier League games for Middlesbrough, Fulham and Chelsea. Saved two penalties in the shoot-out that sent his country to the 2006 World Cup.
Japanese left-back who spent seven years at Inter Milan and also played for Galatasaray and Marseille. Appeared at four World Cups. Famous for his stamina and punishing abdominal training.
Japanese forward signed by Liverpool from Red Bull Salzburg in 2020 after impressing against them in Europe. Later joined Monaco. Versatile across the entire front line.
South Korean forward who joined Wolves from RB Leipzig in 2021. Earlier starred at Red Bull Salzburg alongside a young Erling Haaland. Nicknamed the Bull for his physical running.
American striker who became such a Fulham favourite that the club named a bar after him. Played on with a bloodied face after an elbow from Daniele De Rossi at the 2006 World Cup.
American goalkeeper whose extraordinary display shut out Brazil in a 1998 Gold Cup match, drawing lavish praise from Romario. Played for Millwall, Leicester, Rayo Vallecano and Tottenham.
American midfielder nicknamed Captain America who played for Rangers, Sunderland and Manchester City. Named in the all-star team at the 2002 World Cup. Later became a sporting director in MLS.
